subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI fix disruptive scroll jumps by adding TUI-owned viewport/follow policy, by patching or upgrading pi-tui rendering, or by adding an explicit TUI auto-scroll setting?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the durable fix crosses terminal UX policy and third-party renderer ownership rather than being a narrow code-only repair.

options.title: Repair renderer and anchor behavior
options.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven full redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then only follows new output when the user is already at the tail.

options.title: Add a TUI auto-scroll setting
options.body: Expose an explicit terminal preference if maintainers want user control, accepting the extra settings surface and fresh/upgrade proof burden.

options.title: Hold for live repro first
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until a current-main PTY capture demonstrates the exact jump and renderer reason.

recommendation.title: Repair renderer and anchor behavior
recommendation.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven full redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then only follows new output when the user is already at the tail.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the current TUI source snapshot and pi-tui integration history, so they are the best available owner for the product/ownership choice.
